saml.description: If the SAML identity provider configuration leaves Identity Provider Entity ID empty, Keycloak performs no Issuer validation on received SAML assertions.
saml.note: This can look like issuer-mismatch acceptance but is documented behavior when issuer binding is unset.

saml.description: Brokered usernames may be lower-cased unless case-sensitive username is enabled on the identity provider.
saml.note: Avoid flagging lowercase normalization alone as an identity collision.

saml.description: When Trust Email is enabled, Keycloak trusts email addresses from the external identity provider and may mark them verified during federation.
saml.note: Email-based linking or verification effects may be administrator-authorized behavior, not a bug.

saml.description: During first broker login, Keycloak may create a new local user, link to an existing account, or require confirmation/re-authentication depending on the configured first login flow.
saml.note: Identity merge outcomes can be by-design consequences of the selected first-login flow.

saml.description: When Trust Email is enabled, brokered email addresses are trusted and may be marked verified on first and subsequent logins depending on sync mode.
saml.note: Email-based linking or verification outcomes may be administrator-authorized behavior, not a bug.

saml.description: Admin updates to identity provider certificates, metadata URLs, issuer bindings, or related trust settings are expected to affect subsequent logins.
saml.note: Do not flag changed login outcomes caused by explicit admin trust reconfiguration; only flag continued acceptance of old trust after rotation/cache expiry.

saml.description: Changing SAML metadata URL or validating certificates as an administrator authorizes a new trust anchor for future logins.
saml.note: Do not flag successful login under newly configured trust as stale-cache vulnerability unless the old trust remains accepted unexpectedly after cache expiry.

saml.description: After successful identity-provider login, the browser flow does not continue automatically; extra steps such as MFA must be configured in Post Login Flow.
saml.note: SAML login without MFA is expected unless a post-broker flow enforces MFA.

saml.description: A post login flow can intentionally trigger additional authentication such as OTP after identity provider login.
saml.note: Different MFA behavior between password and SAML paths may be due to configured post-login flow rather than a bypass.

saml.description: If an identity provider is unlinked from an organization, existing organization-group mappers are preserved but inactive; authentication still succeeds and only realm-group mappings continue.
saml.note: Loss of organization-group-derived permissions after unlinking is documented behavior, not an authorization bug.

saml.constraint: For SAML broker testing, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and config.wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing secure configurations. The documentation states that if Identity Provider Entity ID is empty, no Issuer validation is performed, and Validate Signature is a separate switch. Default-config acceptance without these fields is a valid insecure-default test, not a setup mistake.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, config.identity_provider_entity_id supports exact issuer binding only. If this field is empty, no Issuer validation is performed. For multi-identity scenarios, do NOT set it to a wildcard-like value; either set the exact trusted IdP entity ID or omit it entirely to test the no-validation behavior.

For I1 signature trust tests with Use metadata descriptor URL enabled, Keycloak caches downloaded certificates and refresh behavior differs by binding: POST may refresh when a specific certificate is requested and missing; REDIRECT refreshes only after cache expiry. After trust-anchor changes, the fuzzer MUST account for metadata/public-key cache behavior before concluding stale trust acceptance.

For all SAML login tests, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve InResponseTo/RelayState coherence. Keycloak's broker flow is SP-initiated at /realms/{realm}/broker/{broker-alias}/login and the ACS endpoint consumes the resulting response. Sending a fabricated unsolicited response without flow initiation can fail for session reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I2 replay tests, SAML assertions with OneTimeUse and repeated Assertion IDs should be tested with a control successful login first, then a second submission reusing the same assertion identifier. SAML replay protections are expected in SAML contexts; unlike stateless JWTs, replay here is security-relevant.

For I2 expired assertion tests, include a control SAML login without expired_assertion first. A failed expired assertion login alone is ambiguous because Keycloak authentication sessions expire after about 30 minutes by default and other browser/session issues can also cause failure.

Authentication sessions usually expire after 30 minutes by default (Login timeout). Multi-step SAML/browser tests MUST complete within the authentication-session lifetime or refresh the flow. Otherwise, failures may be caused by expired authentication session rather than the SAML property under test.

For I3 config-change tests, admin changes to identity provider trust settings, issuer bindings, or client settings are BY DESIGN and should take effect for new logins. A valid coherence test must show that OLD trust material is still accepted after explicit rotation/update and after any relevant cache window, not merely that behavior changed after an admin update.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, additional authentication after broker login is only enforced if a Post login flow is configured on the identity provider. If Post login flow is unset, successful SAML login without MFA may be expected configuration rather than a bypass. The fuzzer MUST configure post_login_flow_alias to require MFA before testing bypass claims.

For I4 account-linking and collision tests, Keycloak's first broker login flow may create a new user, link an existing one, or require confirmation depending on First Login Flow authenticators. The fuzzer MUST control firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias and trustEmail settings; otherwise identity merges or prompts may reflect configured linking workflow rather than principal-binding flaws.

Trust Email materially affects account-linking semantics. When Trust Email is ON, Keycloak trusts email addresses from the identity provider and may mark them verified on federation. For unverified_email_account_linking tests, the fuzzer MUST set trust_email=false or otherwise account for this by-design trust path; leaving it enabled can cause merges that are configuration-authorized.

Case-sensitive username behavior is configurable per identity provider. If case-sensitive username is disabled, the federated username is lower-cased even though internal usernames are always lower-case. For case-confusion I4 tests, the fuzzer MUST record whether case-sensitive username is enabled; lowercasing alone is not evidence of identity collapse.

For I5 SAML audience tests, the SAML client Client ID is the expected issuer value in AuthnRequests and audience/recipient-related settings are derived from client configuration such as Master SAML Processing URL and ACS URLs. The fuzzer MUST configure the SAML client precisely before testing wrong-audience or missing-conditions cases, or failures may stem from client endpoint mismatch rather than audience enforcement.

Assertion Lifespan has no documented disable sentinel; if not specified, the realm Access Token Lifespan is used. Do not assume 0 disables assertion expiry. Tests that rely on assertion validity windows should set an explicit client assertion lifespan or account for realm defaults.

Password policy Hashing iterations uses sentinel -1 to mean 'use algorithm default iterations', not disable hashing. Do not interpret -1 as off. Exact defaults depend on algorithm (for example argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000).
Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses sentinel 0 to mean 'always re-authenticate before password update', not 'no limit'. Never assume 0 disables the check.
User session count limiter uses sentinel 0 to disable the realm/client session-count check. This is a configuration sentinel, not a literal zero-session allowance.

Authentication session sub-session limit authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 per root authentication session; when reached, the oldest authentication sub-session is removed. High-volume parallel browser/SAML tests in one browser context can evict older sub-sessions and cause misleading flow failures.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, config.identity_provider_entity_id is exact-match issuer binding. If this field is empty, no Issuer validation is performed. To test saml_issuer_mismatch correctly, configure a trusted idpEntityId for the control case; to test insecure defaults, omit it and verify whether login succeeds with arbitrary Issuer.

For SAML signature trust-anchor tests, if config.useMetadataDescriptorUrl=true, Keycloak downloads and caches validating certificates from the metadata URL. Signature validation behavior may change after cache refresh based on metadata cacheDuration/validUntil or cache provider settings. Do NOT interpret acceptance of a newly rotated cert as stale-trust vulnerability unless cache lifetime should already have expired.

For I3 config-change tests involving SAML IdP certificates or metadata URL, admin-initiated trust-anchor changes are BY DESIGN and expected to take effect for new logins. Only flag a violation if the OLD certificate/issuer remains accepted after the configuration was changed and any relevant metadata/public-key cache lifetime has expired.

Principal selection for brokered SAML is controlled by config.principalType and config.principalAttribute. Principal Type can use Subject NameID or a SAML attribute by name/friendly name. For I4 multi-identity tests, keep this configuration fixed and explicit; changing principal source changes the identity-binding semantics and can create false positives.

If config.principalType uses Subject NameID, NameID format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient cannot be used together with Subject NameID value as principal. Do not configure transient NameID when testing stable principal binding, or identity correlation results will be invalid by design.

The general IdP setting Essential claim value supports regular expression format, while Essential claim name matching is case-sensitive. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, do not assume wildcard semantics on other SAML config fields; only this essential-claim value is documented as regex-capable. Exact-match-only fields must be omitted rather than set to '*'.

Case-sensitive username is a broker setting that only affects the username associated with the federated identity; usernames in Keycloak are always lower-case. For I4 case_confusion tests, a difference in local username casing may be by design unless the federated identity/session note itself is collapsed unexpectedly.

Trust Email causes Keycloak to trust email addresses from the identity provider and can mark email as verified on first federation and on subsequent logins when sync mode is FORCE. For unverified_email_account_linking tests, disable Trust Email or results may reflect administrator-authorized trust configuration rather than a vulnerability.

First Login Flow determines whether existing local accounts are linked, created, or require verification. Auto-linking flows such as Automatically Set Existing User are explicitly documented as dangerous and can intentionally link by email/username without prompting. For I4 account-linking tests, use the default first broker login flow or another verification-preserving flow unless you are specifically testing dangerous auto-link behavior.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, additional MFA after broker login is enforced through Post login flow, not automatically by the browser flow after IdP authentication. A valid test MUST configure the IdP's Post Login Flow to include the MFA step; otherwise successful SAML login without MFA is expected by configuration, not a bypass.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. SAML broker flows are session-bound; the executor must initiate the SAML flow and submit a response tied to the current authentication session/InResponseTo. Reusing stale flow state can cause failures unrelated to the invariant under test.

Keycloak may automatically restart authentication in other browser tabs after one tab authenticates, due to shared authentication session behavior. For I3 flow-coherence tests, do not use parallel browser tabs as evidence of inconsistent evaluation; use the same request sequence in a controlled single flow.

For SAML step-up tests using RequestedAuthnContext, if no requested ClassRefs/DeclRefs are present, the Identity Provider does not enforce additional constraints. Therefore, any test expecting stronger authentication MUST include explicit RequestedAuthnContext values or a configured minimum ACR value on the SAML client.

Requested AuthnContext Comparison supports Exact, Minimum, Maximum, or Better. Tests that compare requested vs achieved authentication strength must account for this comparison mode; Exact is the default, but non-Exact modes intentionally allow different satisfying contexts and can otherwise look like authorization overgrant.

SAML client Valid Redirect URIs allow wildcards only at the end of a URL pattern. If ACS URLs are not explicitly registered and are taken from requests, redirect validation follows these patterns. For audience/recipient tests, ensure the control client configuration uses precise redirect/ACS URLs to avoid false positives from permissive wildcard registration.

Include OneTimeUse Condition on a SAML client controls whether Keycloak as IdP emits OneTimeUse in responses. This is not a broker-side replay defense for inbound external assertions. Do not use this client setting as evidence that inbound SAML assertion replay is enforced by the broker.

Assertion Lifespan on a SAML client controls the NotOnOrAfter in assertions Keycloak issues as IdP. It does not configure acceptance lifetime for inbound brokered assertions. Do not treat client-side assertion lifespan settings as broker-side freshness validation knobs.

User session count limiter uses numeric sentinel 0 to disable the check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Never assume 0 means zero sessions allowed; it means no limit is enforced.
Password policy Maximum Authentication Age uses numeric sentinel 0 to require always re-authenticate before password update. This is strict mode, not disable. Do not interpret 0 as unlimited age.

Password policy Hashing iterations uses numeric sentinel -1 to use the default iteration count for the selected algorithm, not literal negative or zero work. Defaults are algorithm-specific (argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000).
WebAuthn Timeout uses numeric sentinel 0 to defer timeout behavior to the authenticator/browser implementation. Do not assume 0 disables timeout checks in a deterministic way.

Client secret rotation uses numeric sentinel Rotated Secret Expiration=0 to remove the old secret immediately during rotation. This is not 'use default'. Tests relying on overlap between old and new secrets must set a positive rotated-secret expiration.

The authenticationSessions SPI authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 sub-sessions per root authentication session; when the limit is reached, the oldest authentication sub-session is removed. High-volume parallel SAML-flow tests can evict older sub-sessions and cause unrelated failures. Keep concurrent unfinished auth flows below the configured limit.

For SAML broker tests of signature validation (I1), create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and config.wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing hardened configurations. The documentation states that if 'Identity Provider Entity ID' is empty, no Issuer validation is performed, and signature validation is controlled by explicit switches.

For insecure-default SAML tests, create_provider with default config MUST leave config.validateSignature and config.wantAssertionsSigned unset/off. The saml_cert_substitution and unsigned-assertion attack patterns rely on observing whether Keycloak accepts forged assertions under default broker settings.

For saml_issuer_mismatch (I1), create_provider/modify_role_config MUST set config.idpEntityId to the trusted IdP entity ID for enforcement tests. If config.idpEntityId is empty, the documentation says no Issuer validation is performed, so acceptance of a wrong Issuer is by configuration, not a vulnerability.

SAML broker login is SP-initiated. saml_login MUST use the broker ACS endpoint /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider}/endpoint with POST form fields SAMLResponse and RelayState, and MUST initiate the SAML flow first so the fabricated response contains a matching InResponseTo.

For I2 replay tests, use TWO saml_login events with the SAME fixed_assertion_id. SAML assertion ID replay detection is the relevant freshness property for SAML; do not treat generic stateless token replay expectations from JWT as applicable here.

For saml_one_time_use_replay (I2), include_onetimeuse=true and fixed_assertion_id must be reused across both saml_login calls. First login should succeed and second should fail; otherwise OneTimeUse is not enforced.

For saml_expired_assertion (I2), the sequence MUST include a control saml_login without expired_assertion=true before the attack login. Without a control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken provider/client setup.

For SAML audience tests (I5), create_application MUST configure the SAML client with a stable Client ID / issuer and ACS URL so the forged assertion can target either the correct or wrong audience. Keycloak matches the issuer from AuthnRequests to the client by Client ID, and SAML assertions carry audience restrictions against the SP/client.

For SAML step-up / RequestedAuthnContext tests, RequestedAuthnContext Comparison supports Exact, Minimum, Maximum, or Better. The default is Exact. Do not assume wildcard or regex semantics for AuthnContext values; they are explicit URI lists, not patterns.

Principal binding for SAML brokered users depends on Principal Type and Principal Attribute. For I4 multi-identity tests, if Principal Type is configured to use a specific SAML attribute, different assertions that share that attribute may intentionally map to the same local account. To test NameID-based separation, configure principalType to Subject NameID and avoid attribute-based principal collapse.

Case-sensitive username behavior is configurable. If 'Case-sensitive username' is disabled, brokered usernames are lower-cased when federating users, while server usernames are always lower-case. I4 case-confusion tests MUST account for lowercasing as by-design normalization unless the setting is enabled.

Trust Email changes account-linking risk. If the identity provider has Trust Email ON and first-login flow permits automatic linking, an external IdP email may be treated as verified. I4 unverified-email-account-linking tests MUST set trustEmail=false or use a flow that requires verification/re-authentication; otherwise linking by trusted email may be administrator-authorized behavior.

First Login Flow materially changes account-linking semantics. The default flow checks for existing email/username collisions and may require confirmation, email verification, or re-authentication. AutoLink / Automatically Set Existing User is explicitly documented as dangerous and can intentionally auto-link accounts. I4 takeover tests must distinguish default safe flow from intentionally unsafe custom flow.

Post Login Flow can intentionally add MFA after brokered login. For saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule (I3), a valid test must compare the same user under password login versus SAML login while ensuring the IdP's Post Login Flow is either configured to enforce MFA or intentionally absent. Otherwise differing MFA behavior may be due to configured flow differences, not a bypass.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. Multi-step browser/SAML sequences that wait too long between SP initiation and saml_login may fail due to expired authentication session rather than security enforcement.

Authentication session sub-session count has a numeric sentinel-like limit: authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 sub-sessions per root authentication session, and when the limit is reached the oldest sub-session is removed. High-volume multi-tab or repeated SP-initiated login tests should avoid exhausting this limit, or failures may reflect eviction rather than protocol rejection.

User session count limiter uses numeric sentinel 0 = disabled for both realm session limit and client session limit. Never interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions. If enabled with 'Deny new session', repeated login attempts in a sequence may be rejected for session-limit reasons unrelated to the tested invariant.

SAML client Assertion Lifespan has sentinel behavior: if not specified, the realm Access Token Lifespan is used. Do not assume an omitted value means no expiry. Freshness tests against assertion validity must set an explicit lifespan or account for realm defaults.

Password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses sentinel 0 = always require re-authentication before password update. Do not interpret 0 as disable. This matters for password-based admin setup or re-authentication flows used during first-broker-login linking.
Password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses sentinel -1 = use algorithm default iterations, not disable hashing. Do not treat -1 as no verification.

WebAuthn/WebAuthn Passwordless timeout uses sentinel 0 = authenticator/browser-dependent timeout behavior, not immediate expiry disable. Tests involving MFA or passkey post-login behavior should not assume 0 means no timeout.

OTP policy 'Reusable code' defaults to disallow reuse. TOTP may still be reusable within the valid time interval depending on policy, while HOTP changes after successful login. MFA-related replay observations must be interpreted in light of OTP policy, not as SAML replay behavior.

For verify_granted_identity after brokered SAML login, the session token MUST be the Keycloak access_token obtained from exchange_code_for_token, not the upstream SAML assertion or any id_token. UserInfo requires a Keycloak bearer access token.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
